catalog_upserts.name: AceFF

catalog_upserts.name: BEND 2.0
catalog_upserts.description: Benchmark that tests whether genomic models predict the effects of DNA changes and can guide sequence design. It has eight tasks on five experimental datasets: hidden-base recovery, splicing effects, cell-type contrast, tissue identity, genetic-background interactions, single-edit ranking, and cell-selective and multi-cell design. Models are scored through linear readouts fitted to frozen embeddings or through their native outputs, with a public leaderboard.
catalog_upserts.status: Open benchmark code (MIT; GitHub). PyPI package bend2 declares MIT AND CC-BY-4.0 AND CC-BY-NC-4.0 because it bundles smaller datasets. No model weights of its own.
catalog_upserts.io: DNA sequence panels + model frozen embeddings, native outputs or nucleotide probabilities -> per-task metrics (splicing and regulatory effect correlations, tissue identification, edit ranking, design utility) and a combined leaderboard score
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Comparing genomic language and sequence-to-function models (e.g. AlphaGenome, NTv3, Evo 2, Enformer, GENERATORv2, DNABERT-2) on variant- and edit-effect prediction and regulatory DNA design

Same family as BEND (bfm-bend), with overlapping authors and the same acronym, but a different paper, repo, package and task set; kept as a separate record, and the curator may add a cross-reference. Data not downloaded.

catalog_upserts.name: THUNDER
catalog_upserts.description: Tile-level benchmark for digital-pathology foundation models (NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks). It compares downstream task performance, feature spaces, robustness and the calibration of predictions built on frozen embeddings. The paper compares 23 pathology and general-vision models on 16 datasets. The pip-installable CLI accepts user-defined models and custom datasets and has since added more models and datasets (including SPIDER), with public leaderboards that are still being updated.
catalog_upserts.status: Benchmark code, CLI and PyPI package thunder-bench under CC BY 4.0, a content licence rather than a software licence. No model weights of its own. The CLI downloads datasets from their original hosts under their own terms, and several are non-commercial: BACH (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0); ESCA, SegPath and TCGA-uniform (Zenodo 'other-nc'); SPIDER (CC BY-NC 4.0, gated on Hugging Face). MHIST requires a data-access form, and STARC-9 declares no licence. Evaluated models are third-party checkpoints, several gated or non-commercial. Public leaderboards. Non-commercial terms apply.
catalog_upserts.io: Histopathology image tiles (built-in or custom datasets) + pathology or general-vision foundation model (built-in or user-defined) -> kNN/linear-probe/few-shot classification, segmentation and zero-shot VLM performance, feature-space comparisons, robustness and calibration metrics (ECE and related errors), leaderboards
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Choosing a pathology foundation model (UNI, Virchow, H-optimus, CONCH, Phikon, Midnight and others) for tile-level tasks; checking robustness and the calibration of embedding-based predictions alongside accuracy; benchmarking a new pathology encoder against the published leaderboards
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-11-06. Checked the arXiv abstract (v3), GitHub API (repo, licence, releases), the README, the dataset loader code, PyPI JSON and the leaderboard page. Upstream dataset terms were checked in the Zenodo records API and the Hugging Face datasets API. noncommercial=true because benchmark datasets the CLI downloads carry NC terms (BACH, ESCA, SegPath, TCGA-uniform, SPIDER), not because of the benchmarked encoders' own terms. Limits: NeurIPS 2025 D&B spotlight comes from the arXiv comment, the README and an OpenReview API listing; the proceedings page was not checked. Licences of BRACS, BreakHis, PanNuke, WILDS, OCELOT and MHIST were not each confirmed. Not executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Patho-Bench
catalog_upserts.description: Mahmood Lab Python library and canonical train/test splits for benchmarking computational-pathology patch and slide encoders on 95 slide- and patient-level tasks from 33 public datasets, with linear probing, retrieval, Cox survival prediction and supervised fine-tuning.
catalog_upserts.status: Code CC BY-NC 4.0; task splits on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (not gated); slide data from original sources under their own terms; no own model weights. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact.
catalog_upserts.io: Trident-extracted patch embeddings from pathology foundation models (pooled to slide/patient level by Patho-Bench) + task splits -> linear-probe, retrieval, survival (c-index) and fine-tuning metrics
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Comparing pathology patch and slide encoders with fixed splits on morphological subtyping, tumour-microenvironment, grading, molecular subtyping, mutation prediction, treatment response and survival tasks
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint only; the arXiv paper covers the Trident + Patho-Bench tool suite and reports 42 public tasks, while the current README and HF release list 95 tasks across 33 datasets. GitHub's licence API reports NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file is CC BY-NC 4.0. HF splits are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and not gated (gated=false; files fetch without login), although the card YAML keeps inactive gating text citing CC-BY-NC 4.0 and no redistribution. Not the same resource as PathBench (birkhoffkiki). Last code push 2025-11-07. Upstream slide-dataset terms were not reviewed.

catalog_upserts.name: FLIP
catalog_upserts.description: Protein fitness benchmark with curated train/test splits that test how well sequence-based models, including protein language model embeddings, generalise under realistic domain shifts. FLIP (2021) covers AAV capsid viability, GB1 binding and Meltome thermostability, and the repo adds per-residue/property sets (bind, cas, conservation, sav, scl, secondary_structure). FLIP2 (2026) adds seven datasets (amylase, imine reductase, NucB, TrpB, hydrophobic core, rhodopsin, PDZ3) with 16 splits and zero-shot, ridge and fine-tuned pLM baselines.
catalog_upserts.status: Code and baselines under Academic Free License 3.0 (GitHub). Split data on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0; the project site says data are under CC BY 4.0 or MIT per dataset README, with upstream assay terms recorded there. Legacy raw data are on a public server with no stated licence. No model weights (benchmark).
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequences (mutant libraries, protein families) with fitness and other protein property labels -> model embeddings or predictions scored on defined train/test splits
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Evaluating protein language model embeddings and simpler baselines for fitness prediction and extrapolation under engineering-relevant splits (mutation-, position-, fitness-level- and wild-type-based); comparison against legacy FLIP results
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Both papers are preprints according to the bioRxiv API and Crossref. The README says FLIP was submitted to the NeurIPS 2021 benchmark track, and the FLIP2 site claims ICML 2026 (Spotlight); neither proceedings listing was checked. FLIP2 was merged into the original repo (commit 'FLIPv2 release', 2026-03-03; PR #27 merged 2026-04-23). The README asks users not to report performance on splits marked obsolete. Upstream source-assay terms were checked only for meltome ('Free for anyone to use'); other dataset READMEs were not read. The legacy raw-data server states no licence.

catalog_upserts.name: PoseBusters
catalog_upserts.description: Python test suite of chemical and physical plausibility checks for predicted protein-ligand poses and generated molecules, released with the PoseBusters Benchmark set (428 PDB complexes; the journal results use a 308-complex subset) and the Astex Diverse set. The paper reports that none of the five deep-learning docking methods tested outperformed classical docking tools on physical plausibility or generalisation to novel protein sequences. PoseBusters is also the optional ligand-validation step in PLINDER evaluation.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code (GitHub; PyPI posebusters); paper benchmark data on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0; no own model weights.
catalog_upserts.io: Predicted protein-ligand complex poses or generated molecules (+ optional reference ligand and protein structures) -> chemical/physical validity checks and pose-accuracy success rates
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Checking the physical validity of predicted protein-ligand poses from docking and co-folding methods, and of generated molecules; comparing methods on the PoseBusters benchmark set
catalog_upserts.audit_note: year=2023 is the arXiv first version (2023-08-10) and the Zenodo data date; Crossref lists the journal issue as 2024. The RSC landing page returns 403 to scripted clients; Crossref and arXiv confirm the article. On the 2026-11-06 re-check the Zenodo record answered 200 for both HTML and API, and its latest version is this 2023 record. PyPI metadata has no licence field; the licence comes from GitHub (MIT). PDB source terms were not reviewed. Scope is protein-ligand pose evaluation: a benchmark for structure/co-folding models, not a model.

catalog_upserts.name: PLINDER
aliases: Protein Ligand INteraction Dataset and Evaluation Resource
catalog_upserts.description: Versioned dataset and evaluation resource of PDB-derived protein-ligand systems (and, in current releases, protein-protein interfaces) with annotations, similarity clusters, linked apo/predicted structures and an evaluation harness for docking and co-folding models. The 2024 preprint releases provide leakage-aware train/validation/test splits; it was used for the NeurIPS 2024 MLSB challenge. Releases are versioned by RCSB snapshot month (current 2026-09, which provides cluster and set-cover sampling tables rather than fixed splits).
catalog_upserts.status: Code Apache-2.0; PLINDER-curated data Apache-2.0, BindingDB-curated data CC BY 4.0 and ChEMBL-imported data CC BY-SA 4.0 (per README). Current release on a public file server, no gating; historical 2024 split releases on a Google Cloud bucket (not checked). No model weights.
catalog_upserts.io: PDB-derived protein-ligand systems and protein-protein interfaces + predicted complexes -> annotation, similarity and cluster tables, split/sampling sets, and lDDT/RMSD/PoseBusters evaluation metrics
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Training and leakage-aware evaluation of protein-ligand docking and co-folding models; similarity-stratified test sets; selecting diverse training representatives
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-reviewed 2026-11-06. Preprint only (bioRxiv v3, 2024-07-19, CC BY; no journal version per bioRxiv API). README states PLINDER-curated data Apache-2.0, BindingDB CC BY 4.0, ChEMBL CC BY-SA 4.0; upstream wwPDB terms not re-checked. Code was GPL-2.0 between 2026-02-19 and 2026-04-13, Apache-2.0 since (PyPI 1.0.0, 2026-10-09). The 2026-09 CAMEO release has no splits directory; fixed splits are in the 2024 releases on gs://plinder, whose anonymous listing returned HTTP 401 (objects not tested). Files were listed, not downloaded.

catalog_upserts.name: BILBY-PRO
catalog_upserts.description: Motif-scaffolding benchmark of 220 structurally conserved functional motifs (174 PROSITE patterns) derived from PROSITE-linked experimental structures for evaluating generative protein-design models, paired with BILBY-MD, a reference-based all-atom molecular-dynamics evaluation framework (applied in the paper to statically solved MotifBench designs) that tests whether designs keep motif and scaffold geometry over simulation time.
catalog_upserts.status: Benchmark data CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face (not gated), except verbatim PROSITE pattern strings, whose source is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and PDB-derived structures under their upstream terms; construction and MD-evaluation code Apache-2.0; no own model weights. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one component.
catalog_upserts.io: Motif-scaffolding problems (motif PDBs, contigs) + generated scaffolds -> static success and unique-solution metrics (via the MotifBench evaluation pipeline); MD-based motif/scaffold drift, motif-contact preservation and motif-dihedral free-energy comparisons against reference simulations
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Comparing scaffold-generation models (RFDiffusion, Proteina, ESM3 and others) on a broader, systematically derived motif set; testing dynamical stability of designs beyond static refolding
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint posted 2026-11-05; NeurIPS 2026 E&D acceptance from the arXiv comment and HF card only. HF dataset created 2026-11-02 and still contains .pytest_cache files; card DOI 10.57967/hf/11443 resolves to the dataset page. noncommercial=true reflects the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 PROSITE pattern strings that the card says are not relicensed. Card notes a fresh reconstruction has not been validated. BILBY-MD has no tagged release and its job scripts target SLURM/GROMACS on JSC systems. Data not downloaded.

catalog_upserts.name: PRISM benchmark (pathology)
catalog_upserts.description: Tile-level benchmark that measures the reliability of pathology foundation models jointly along model choice, label fraction (1-100%), calibration and cross-institution transfer, with frozen-embedding linear-probe reference results for eight models on six datasets and a five-hospital Camelyon17 shift study.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code (PyPI prism-bench 0.3.0); precomputed embeddings for five models on Hugging Face under CC BY-NC 4.0 behind an auto-approved gate that asks for name and affiliation and agreement to non-commercial, non-clinical use; UNI, CONCH and Virchow2 embeddings and the MHIST dataset are recipe-only (not redistributed); upstream model and dataset licences apply; no own model weights.
catalog_upserts.io: Frozen tile-level embeddings from a pathology FM (user-extracted, or the gated precomputed set) on the PRISM datasets -> linear-probe AUROC, calibration (ECE, temperature scaling) and out-of-distribution transfer metrics across label fractions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Comparing pathology foundation models for low-label tile classification; checking calibration and cross-hospital transfer of frozen embeddings in research settings
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Single-author workshop paper (Third GenAI4Health Workshop at NeurIPS 2026, per arXiv comment), preprint only; package at its first PyPI release 0.3.0; repo has no tagged releases. Embeddings gated (name/affiliation form, auto-approved, CC BY-NC 4.0, non-clinical); gate not accepted and RELEASE_POLICY.md not read. Same name as the unrelated Paige PRISM models (bfm-prism, bfm-prism2): display with qualifier.

catalog_upserts.name: spora
catalog_upserts.description: Harmonized multimodal spatial-proteomics resource (13,546 standardized multiplex images, 5,477 patients, 35 cohorts, five technologies, with tissue/cell segmentations, clinical metadata and paired H&E where available), a Python data interface (spora [io]), and a benchmark suite (spora [bench]) that compares spatial-proteomics foundation models such as VirTues and KRONOS with task-specific baselines. The suite covers twelve cohorts, with tasks in cell phenotyping, cross-cohort cell segmentation and annotation, tissue-level diagnostic/therapeutic prediction, and multiplex and H&E-to-multiplex virtual staining.
catalog_upserts.status: Benchmark code (spora-bench) CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; data interface (spora-io) MIT. Data openly downloadable without sign-in from the BioImage Archive (anonymous S3/rclone), with per-cohort licences: mostly CC BY 4.0, three CC0 1.0, one CC BY-NC 4.0 (klein2026explainable), one without a licence file (lin2022multiplexed). No model weights of its own; evaluated models (e.g. VirTues, KRONOS) come under their own terms. Non-commercial terms apply to the benchmark code and to one cohort.
catalog_upserts.io: Multiplexed spatial-proteomics images (IMC, CODEX, MIBI, Orion, IF; paired H&E where available) plus foundation-model representations or task-specific model outputs -> cell phenotyping, segmentation/annotation, tissue-level prediction and virtual-staining metrics
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Evaluating spatial-proteomics foundation models (for example VirTues, KRONOS) against task-specific baselines across cohorts and marker panels; cross-cohort generalization tests; harmonized multi-cohort data for pretraining spatial-proteomics models
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint (arXiv 2026-10-15); NeurIPS 2026 E&D-track acceptance is self-reported in the arXiv comment and repo BibTeX, with no proceedings page checked. Licences read from the LICENSE files: spora-bench CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, spora-io MIT (GitHub shows NOASSERTION because the header was modified). Per-cohort LICENSE files read from the public BioImage Archive S3 bucket on 2026-11-06: 30 CC BY 4.0, 3 CC0, 1 CC BY-NC 4.0, 1 missing (lin2022multiplexed, whose prefix listed no files). Data presence checked by anonymous bucket listing only; nothing was downloaded. The spatial lane may also propose this resource; keep one record.

catalog_upserts.name: TriProRep
catalog_upserts.description: Family of structure-aware protein encoders (35M to 3B parameters) pretrained with an ELECTRA-style corrective masked-token objective over three aligned per-residue token streams: amino-acid identity plus backbone and local full-atom geometry discretized by VQ-VAE tokenizers. The released encoders are reused frozen as conditioning or alignment features, including as the structure-representation component of the K-Fold co-folding model.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code; MIT, ungated weights in four sizes (35M-3B); a 3B fine-tuned encoder is also released ungated but its card states no licence; tokenized pretraining corpus published under MIT and RepSP benchmark under CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face
catalog_upserts.io: Protein structure (PDB file, one chain) -> per-residue structure-aware embeddings (480- to 2560-dim depending on size) or discrete sequence/backbone/full-atom tokens
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Conditioning or frozen features for co-folding and structure prediction, residue-level interaction-property prediction, protein representation probing
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Code licence read from LICENSE (MIT text plus a note that adapted SimpleFold/Boltz code is MIT; this note is why GitHub reports NOASSERTION). Weight licence for 35M/150M/650M/3B from HF card metadata ('license: mit'); triprorep-3B-finetune card has no licence statement. Data licences are HF dataset-card declarations (triprorep-pretrain MIT; repsp-benchmark CC BY 4.0, AFDB-derived); upstream terms of the structures behind the tokenized pretraining corpus not reviewed. Parameter counts and embedding dimensions are the authors' claims; nothing was downloaded or run. Cross-lane duplicate in the protein lane not checked by this reviewer.

catalog_upserts.name: Bolero
catalog_upserts.description: Cell-state-conditioned sequence-to-function model (Harvard/Arc Institute; Liu, Zhou, Greenberg) that adds conditional low-rank adapters, generated from atlas-scale cell-state embeddings, to a frozen Flashzoi (Borzoi) backbone; trained on Bolero-10M (10.7M cells, 33 single-cell ATAC/multiome datasets, six mammals) to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (MIT code; MIT on Hugging Face card metadata for weights and data), ungated; requires the separately distributed Flashzoi/Borzoi backbone
catalog_upserts.io: 524,288 bp DNA + cell-state embedding (optional tissue, AP-1 score, bulk accessibility track) -> cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance at 32 bp resolution
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Cell-state-specific regulatory-activity prediction, per-cell-type non-coding variant effects (caQTL/eQTL), cross-species prediction, motif grammar and attribution analysis
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery 2026-11-06; adversarial check 2026-11-06. Preprint v1 (2026-10-20), not peer reviewed; preprint text CC BY-NC (paper only). 13 adapter checkpoints on HF; weight and data licences rest on Hugging Face card metadata (no separate LICENSE file in the model repo); terms of the upstream single-cell datasets not reviewed. Adapter checkpoints depend on the Flashzoi/Borzoi backbone. GitHub README gives 10.8M cells/36 datasets vs 10.7M/33 in paper and card. Linux + NVIDIA GPU only. Nothing downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: DeepD
catalog_upserts.description: Phylogeny-informed sparse mixture-of-experts genome language model from China Agricultural University and BioMap Research, pretrained at single-nucleotide resolution on unselected whole genomes from all domains of life and viruses; trained at two scales, DeepD-2B (1.8B parameters, 1T tokens, 8K context) and DeepD-60B (63B parameters, ~1B active, 5.69T tokens, context extended to 1M tokens by midtraining).
catalog_upserts.status: Web/API only: token-gated hosted inference API (embeddings, logits, generation), key free for non-commercial research under CC BY-NC 4.0 (university e-mails auto-activated, others reviewed); prompts up to 9,997 nt, served checkpoint not stated; Apache-2.0 client code and notebooks; notebook assets on Hugging Face without a licence; weights and model source code not released (promised by publication)
catalog_upserts.io: DNA prompt (up to 9,997 nt via the API) + optional species name -> nucleotide-resolution embeddings, per-position logits with loss/perplexity, or species-conditioned generated DNA
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot variant-effect scoring from sequence log-likelihoods, embeddings for downstream sequence classifiers, species-conditioned DNA generation; the preprint also reports promoter design and chromosome-scale generation with its Context-Anchor-Body strategy (not documented as an API workflow)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery and adversarial review 2026-11-06. Preprint v1 (2026-10-18), not peer reviewed. Access only through a key-gated hosted API (non-commercial, CC BY-NC 4.0); gateway endpoint answers 401 without a token, but the API was not exercised and the served checkpoint is undocumented. Weights and model source code promised by publication, not released; re-check at publication.

catalog_upserts.name: USM-AA
catalog_upserts.description: Transformer encoder from Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab and HKUST (Guangzhou), pretrained with reverse-complement masked language modelling on the human reference genome, variant-based sequences from 3,202 1000 Genomes individuals and a multi-species corpus; it places tokens on reference-genome coordinates via alignment-aware rotary positions and an alignment embedding of chromosome, strand and CIGAR.
catalog_upserts.status: Code under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; 100M and 1B weights on public Google Drive links from the repo README with no weight-specific licence (no explicit grant beyond the repo's non-commercial terms); not gated; preprint CC BY-NC 4.0
catalog_upserts.io: DNA sequence aligned to hg38 with minimap2 (chromosome, strand, coordinates, CIGAR) -> contextual embeddings and masked-token predictions; backbone for fine-tuning
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Variant-aware and long-range regulatory sequence modelling (eQTL prediction), cancer-type classification from individual variants, fine-tuning on genomic benchmarks (NT, GUE, Genomic Benchmarks)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06. Preprint v1 (2026-10-12), not peer reviewed. Repo is the first author's personal account, linked from the paper abstract. Weights hosted on Google Drive (file pages resolve anonymously; files not downloaded; Drive owner not verifiable; no versioning). No weight-specific licence; repository licence is PolyForm NC 1.0.0. README's models/download.sh is absent (404). A Hugging Face copy (JimmyYang2025/usmaa_100m, no card) is not linked from repo or paper and is not treated as official.

catalog_upserts.name: Shorkie (Shorkie_LM)
catalog_upserts.description: Calico/Johns Hopkins masked DNA language model (Shorkie_LM) pretrained on 165 Saccharomycetales genomes and its fine-tuned 8-fold sequence-to-expression ensemble (Shorkie) trained on 5,215 yeast RNA-seq and epigenomic tracks, including transcriptional-regulator induction time courses.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code; public ungated weights (CC BY 4.0 per README and docs) on Calico's gs://seqnn-share bucket over HTTPS; training data and the R64 genome copy used by the examples in a requester-pays bucket (GCP billing project needed)
catalog_upserts.io: Fungal/yeast DNA window -> masked-base predictions and embeddings (LM); RNA-seq and genomic coverage tracks and variant-effect scores (fine-tuned ensemble)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Yeast gene-expression prediction, cis-eQTL and MPRA variant-effect scoring, promoter and splicing-signal interpretation, fine-tuning on new yeast RNA-seq
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery 2026-11-06, adversarial verify 2026-11-06. Preprint, not peer reviewed. The v2 landing page links the calico/shorkie-paper repo. Weight files were confirmed by the public bucket listing and an HTTP HEAD request only, not downloaded. Weight licence: CC BY 4.0 per the repository README and the docs Datasets page. The docs License page does not name it. Running the documented examples needs the R64 genome copy from a requester-pays bucket. Unofficial ports and re-uploads (tdsone/shorkie-pytorch, ZiyanZhuang/shorkie-pytorch, ZiyanZhuang Hugging Face repos) are not the official artifact.

catalog_upserts.name: ProkBERT family
catalog_upserts.description: Family of compact BERT-style genomic language models for prokaryotes and microbiomes (prokbert-mini, -mini-long, -mini-c; about 21-27M parameters) using Local Context-Aware (LCA) k-mer tokenization, pretrained on RefSeq genomes of bacteria, archaea, viruses and fungi, with released fine-tuned variants for promoter, phage and phage-lifestyle (PhaStyle) prediction.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code; ungated base weights under CC BY-NC 4.0 (Hugging Face card metadata); non-commercial terms apply to the weights; PhaStyle fine-tunes carry stricter terms (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 / CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per card metadata)
catalog_upserts.io: Prokaryotic DNA segments -> embeddings, masked-token predictions; fine-tuned promoter/phage/lifestyle classifiers
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Microbial promoter identification, phage sequence and lifestyle classification, microbiome sequence representation and transfer learning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery 2026-11-06 (catalog gap, not an in-window release); adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06. bioRxiv preprint 2023-11-13 (Europe PMC PPR759533), journal version 2024-01-12 (Crossref); year set to 2023. Weight licences from HF card metadata only. Small models (mini scale); scope rests on the general base encoders, not the task fine-tunes. PhaStyle fine-tunes are NC-ND / NC-SA. Weights not downloaded.

catalog_upserts.name: DNABERT-S
catalog_upserts.description: Species-aware DNA embedding model built on DNABERT-2 and further trained with manifold-instance mixup and curriculum contrastive learning on about 2 million sequence pairs from viral, fungal and bacterial genomes, so that embeddings cluster sequences by species.
catalog_upserts.status: Ungated weights on Hugging Face with Apache-2.0 in card metadata only (no model-card text); GitHub code has no licence file (all rights reserved by default); training/evaluation data on Google Drive with no stated licence
catalog_upserts.io: DNA sequence -> species-aware embedding
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Species clustering, metagenomic binning, few-shot species classification
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery 2026-11-06 (catalog gap); adversarial verify 2026-11-06 confirmed it with corrections. Journal article confirmed via Crossref and the Europe PMC/PMC full text (CC BY 4.0); academic.oup.com returns 403 to automated fetch. HF checkpoint is on the first author's account and the paper and README endorse it. The weight licence rests on card YAML metadata only; the code repository and the Google Drive data have no licence. Scope is borderline: a species-focused contrastive derivative of DNABERT-2 (bfm-dnabert-2), included as a reusable embedding model used for several species-level tasks.

catalog_upserts.name: AlphaProtein Novo
catalog_upserts.description: Google DeepMind generative diffusion model that co-generates protein backbones and sequences conditioned on a catalytic motif and its ligand context, released for de novo enzyme design via structural motif scaffolding (indexed or unindexed motifs, novel scaffold or partial diffusion). The repository wraps the generator in an optional pipeline with LigandMPNN sequence redesign, AlphaFold 3 (or an AlphaFold 3 Leaving Atom variant) refolding and design-evaluation metrics.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code (all other materials CC-BY 4.0); generator weights downloaded from a Google Cloud Storage bucket under custom non-commercial AP Novo parameter terms: non-commercial organisations only, no redistribution of the weights outside your organisation, outputs under separate Output Terms and not usable to train similar design models, plus a prohibited-use policy and revocable access; optional AlphaFold 3 / AF3 Leaving Atom weights under the AlphaFold 3 parameter terms; training data not released; no API or hosted server
catalog_upserts.io: Catalytic motif and ligand context in a design manifest -> co-generated protein backbone and sequence, optionally redesigned and refolded by the bundled pipeline
catalog_upserts.use_cases: De novo enzyme design, catalytic-motif scaffolding in ligand context, novel-scaffold or partial-diffusion protein generation, design evaluation and ranking pipelines
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarial review 2026-11-06. Identity: bioRxiv v1 (2026-10-05, DOI 10.64898/2026.10.01.756017, corresponding institution Google DeepMind) and the official google-deepmind/alphaprotein-novo repository (fork=false, created 2026-10-05, Apache-2.0) cite each other; weights come from a Google-controlled GCS bucket named in the README, not a mirror. Distinct from AlphaProteo, RFdiffusion, RFdiffusion2 and AlphaFold 3. Artifact: HEAD on generator.bin.zst returned HTTP 200, 547,140,096 bytes, last-modified 2026-09-28; nothing downloaded or run; repo has no tagged releases, so the bucket object is the only weights route. Terms read in full from WEIGHTS_TERMS_OF_USE.md (non-commercial organisations only; no publishing or sharing of parameters outside your organisation; outputs may not train or distill similar de novo design models; prohibited-use policy incorporated; Google may suspend or terminate access and may ask for verification of name and organisation on an access request) — the current download needs no sign-in, but access is revocable. Limits: no model hub card; preprint is unrefereed and its wet-lab design-success claims were not reproduced or independently checked; training data not released; AF3 / AF3-LA and LigandMPNN stages carry separate licences and are not part of this record. Protein-modality discovery may propose the same model under an alias; deduplicate against normalized 'alphaprotein novo' / 'ap novo'.

catalog_upserts.name: SO3LR / SO3LR Tauri
catalog_upserts.description: Machine-learned force-field family that couples an SO3krates message-passing network to explicit physics modules for short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion and electrostatics. The SO3LR Tauri models (sizes S, M, L) are trained on 148 million quantum-chemical structures spanning 85 elements and are bundled with the so3lr package for reactive and biomolecular molecular dynamics; the legacy SO3LR model from the 2025 JACS paper ships alongside them for eight elements.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (MIT); weights bundled in the GitHub repository (installed from source, no tagged release asset or PyPI package): SO3LR Tauri weights CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial, fine-tunes inherit the licence), legacy SO3LR weights MIT; training and test data on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0; ungated, no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Atomic structure (elements, coordinates, optional total charge; periodic or gas phase) -> potential energy and forces (stress optional for periodic cells), through a CLI for optimization, MD and dataset evaluation, an ASE calculator, and fine-tuning and training entry points
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Reactive and biomolecular molecular dynamics (proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, metal-containing biomolecules), ion hydration and side-chain pKa estimation, organic and enzymatic reaction paths, interaction and binding energies, solvent densities, experimental fine-tuning on custom data

catalog_upserts.name: Prompteina
catalog_upserts.description: Text-conditioned all-atom protein structure generator, built by adapting NVIDIA's Proteina-Complexa denoiser with text-conditioned pretraining on a paired corpus of 1.8 million structures and more than 50 million captions. Two frozen Qwen3 encoders embed a free-text prompt that specifies fold and topology, secondary structure, tertiary motifs, global shape, surface properties, interface properties or function; separate monomer and binder checkpoints are released for inference.
catalog_upserts.status: Code Apache-2.0; two ungated inference checkpoints (monomer, binder) on Hugging Face under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which states models are commercially usable and derivatives may be distributed, with NVIDIA Trustworthy AI terms incorporated by reference; repository data assets CC BY 4.0; the repository's root LICENSE is a pointer file, so GitHub reports NOASSERTION. The checkpoints are inference-only and not self-contained: the Proteina-Complexa autoencoder downloads separately through the code repository and the frozen Qwen3 text encoders are fetched from the Hub at build time. The paired text-structure training corpus is announced but not released (its repository holds a placeholder card only), and its licence is unstated.
catalog_upserts.io: Natural-language property description, optionally with a target structure for binder design -> generated all-atom protein structure
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Prompt-specified de novo monomer design across folds, topologies and symmetry; target binder design; design campaigns specified in natural language, including use inside agent-driven design loops as described by the authors

catalog_upserts.name: RFD4-Proteina
catalog_upserts.description: Flow-matching generative model for biomolecular design from the Institute for Protein Design and NVIDIA GenAIR, released as a matched pair of a flow model and the autoencoder it was trained against (435,622,465 stored parameters across the pair, FP32). The unified autoencoder covers proteins, nucleic acids and small molecules with a 147-class residue vocabulary, and one checkpoint pair serves monomer, binder, antibody and nanobody, enzyme and motif-scaffolding and ligand-pocket design with sequence-structure co-design, partial diffusion and reward-guided search. A separate antibody checkpoint and a LoRA adapter over the pretrained base ship alongside it.
catalog_upserts.io: Annotated CIF structures or a YAML condition specification (fixed motifs, hotspots, burial, hydrogen bonds, target chains, ligands) -> designed molecular structures in CIF with generated residue identities and coordinates
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: BSD-3-Clause for the model, weights and code (Copyright 2026, Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington); the Hugging Face weights, the Diffusers port and the training-data repository are ungated. catalog_upserts.name: recAMPLIFY
catalog_upserts.description: Recursive masked protein language model from the AMPLIFY group (Chandar lab, Mila/Polytechnique Montreal, with Amgen): a weight-tied transformer core refines residue-aligned hidden states over an adjustable number of cycles, so inference compute can grow without adding parameters; Gated Mixture Recurrence (GMR) variants make that depth adaptive. The main 155M-parameter checkpoint (recamplify-1m) was pretrained on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M; the hub repository also holds 100K-step recursive and GMR variants (133-134M) and AMPLIFY baselines retrained in this codebase, eleven checkpoints in all.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: code MIT (AMPLIFY repository, recamplify branch); weights MIT per the Hugging Face card, ungated, eleven checkpoints in one repository loaded with trust_remote_code. Pretraining data (UniRef100, SCOP, OAS) not redistributed.
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence -> masked-token logits, with a selectable number of recurrence cycles (GMR variants also report expected cycles); per-residue hidden states for embedding probes via the training/evaluation code
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Protein representation learning, zero-shot mutation-effect scoring, contact recovery, fold, localization, stability and secondary-structure probes, test-time compute scaling studies for pLMs
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 from the arXiv record and HTML full text, the ungated Hugging Face file listing and card, and the AMPLIFY repository recamplify branch (MIT LICENSE on branch). catalog_upserts.name: InstructPro2
catalog_upserts.description: Instruction-following protein design model: a text encoder reads a natural-language function description while frozen ligand (ChemBERTa) and antigen (esm2_t12_35M_UR50D) encoders supply biological context through gated cross-attention adapters to a decoder initialised from ProGen2-large-BFD90, giving a 3.2B-parameter model pretrained on 205.7 million function-description and protein pairs from UniProtKB. Three checkpoints are released: text-conditioned stage 1 (2.87B), a ligand-binding variant and an antibody variant that designs heavy-chain HCDR1-3 (3.22B each).
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights + data: MIT on the repository (LICENSE), the Hugging Face model card and the dataset card; three ungated checkpoints, distributed with the copy of ProGen2-large-BFD90 they require at inference, whose base weights are BSD-3-Clause.
catalog_upserts.io: Natural-language function description, optionally with a ligand SMILES or antigen chains -> protein sequence, scaffold spans, or antibody heavy-chain HCDR1-3
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Text-specified functional protein generation, ligand-binding protein design, antibody CDR design, scaffold infilling from a described function, starting point for further finetuning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 from the arXiv v1 abstract page and full text, the MIT GitHub repository (API license endpoint: MIT) and the ungated Hugging Face model and dataset APIs, including the blob listing that shows the three checkpoints (5.7-6.4 GB each) and the bundled ProGen2-large-BFD90 weights. catalog_upserts.name: AbBFN2
catalog_upserts.description: Antibody foundation model built on the Bayesian Flow Network paradigm, so it jointly models discrete and continuous variables and can condition generation on an arbitrary subset of 45 antibody 'data modes' covering paired heavy and light chain sequences, genetic assignment and biophysical metadata. Every mode is produced at inference, which lets one model serve unconditional generation, sequence inpainting and labelling, humanisation and metadata-conditioned design without task-specific training.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code; ungated weights under the InstaDeep Open Model Licence 1.0, non-commercial use only (serving outputs as a service is excluded; derived or distilled models must stay non-commercial under the same licence). catalog_upserts.io: Any subset of 45 antibody data modes (paired sequences, germline and biophysical metadata) as conditioning -> values for all 45 modes, including generated paired sequences
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Antibody sequence generation, inpainting and labelling, humanisation, germline- and metadata-conditioned de novo library design, biophysical property optimisation

catalog_upserts.name: ProtCell
catalog_upserts.description: Transformer foundation model for single-cell proteomics that combines protein-identity and continuous-abundance embeddings and is pretrained by masked protein-abundance modelling across heterogeneous CITE-seq and CyTOF panels mapped to a shared protein vocabulary; the study assembles about 380 million cells from 98 datasets for pretraining and evaluation.

catalog_upserts.name: S-PLM
catalog_upserts.description: Structure-aware protein language model trained by multi-view contrastive learning that aligns an ESM-2 (650M) sequence encoder with a 3D structure encoder, so sequence-only inference yields structure-aware embeddings. V1 encodes AlphaFold-predicted structures with a Swin-Transformer on contact maps; V2 is an updated residue-level model with a GVP structure encoder. The repository provides lightweight tuning recipes (top-layer fine-tuning, adapters, LoRA) for EC number, Gene Ontology, fold, enzyme-reaction and secondary-structure tasks. A 2026 V3 weights-only posting (frozen ProtT5-XL trunk, TM-calibrated, EC-retrieval and residue-alignment heads) awaits its paper and public code.
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code for V1/V2; pretrained V1 and V2 checkpoints downloadable from author-hosted Google Drive and SharePoint folders, with no licence stated separately for the weights. V3 weights are ungated on Hugging Face under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (no commercial use) but cannot be run yet: the architecture config and inference code sit in a private repository while the V3 paper is in preparation.
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence -> structure-aware protein-level and residue-level embeddings (V1/V2: ESM-2 650M-sized); V3 (when its code is public): 1024-d raw, TM-calibrated and EC-retrieval embeddings plus residue-level alignment features
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Structure-aware protein embeddings without predicted structures, protein clustering and fold classification, EC number and Gene Ontology prediction, enzyme-reaction classification, secondary-structure prediction via lightweight tuning
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06. catalog_upserts.name: AlphaEnzyme
catalog_upserts.description: Enzyme foundation model that builds a structure-grounded joint representation of an enzyme and its reaction and reads out catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response from that shared representation; the shared encoder was pretrained on about 500,000 curated RHEA enzyme-reaction pairs before task supervision. The release reports 30.1% top-1 catalyst retrieval on a time-separated benchmark against 17.2% for the strongest baseline, Michaelis-constant rank correlations up to 0.64 at most 40% identity to the kinetic training set, and enrichment of high-fitness TrpB variants; code, five task checkpoints and the task tables are published in three separate places.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code and ungated weights under non-commercial terms. The repository LICENSE is a short custom agreement citing Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 and adding three restrictions: no commercial use, no use in drug development or discovery (including target, hit or lead identification, candidate selection and lead optimisation), and no use of outputs to train other large language models, protein-structure-prediction technology or similar models; it does not reproduce the CC text and GitHub classifies it NOASSERTION. Neither hub repo carries licence metadata, so these repository terms are the only stated terms for the weights and data. The five released checkpoints are task heads and ensembles: the upstream Protenix and ESM-C weights are not bundled and must be obtained separately, and full inference on new sequences also needs P2Rank/Java and a CUDA GPU. Third-party runtimes keep their own licences (Protenix, OpenFold, TorchDrug Apache-2.0; P2Rank MIT). The preprint is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and the competing-interests statement records that the industrial partner holds exclusive commercialisation rights to the models, code and results.
catalog_upserts.io: Enzyme amino-acid sequence plus a reaction as canonical or atom-mapped SMILES -> catalyst retrieval ranking, log10 kcat and log10 Km predictions, and variant-activity ranking within a submitted library (the structure-grounded representation is computed internally)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Enzyme retrieval for a target reaction, kinetic parameter prediction, enzyme variant prioritisation and directed-evolution triage
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from the preprint (landing page, bioRxiv API record and full PDF), the GitHub repository metadata, README, LICENSE and configs, and the ungated Hugging Face model and dataset listings. catalog_upserts.name: RigidSSL
catalog_upserts.description: Two-phase geometric self-supervised pretraining framework for protein structure generation that represents backbones as residue-level rigid bodies in SE(3) and trains an AlphaFold2-style IPA encoder with a bidirectional, rigidity-aware flow-matching objective. Phase I (RigidSSL-Perturb) learns geometric priors from 432K AlphaFold DB structures with simulated perturbations; Phase II (RigidSSL-MD) refines them on 1.3K ATLAS molecular dynamics trajectories. The released checkpoints are used to warm-start the IPA modules of downstream generators (FrameDiff, FoldFlow-2, AlphaFlow); the paper reports designability gains of up to 43%, a 5.8% higher zero-shot motif-scaffolding success rate and more realistic GPCR conformational ensembles.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: code MIT; both phase checkpoints labelled MIT on an ungated Hugging Face repo. Processed pretraining data is ungated and labelled MIT, but the Phase II data derives from the ATLAS MD database, which is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); AlphaFold DB upstream terms for Phase I data not checked. Repository provides pretraining code only; downstream finetuning requires integrating the weights into FrameDiff/FoldFlow-2/AlphaFlow. No API or hosted route.
catalog_upserts.io: Protein backbone structures as residue-level rigid frames (static structures or MD conformation pairs) -> pretrained IPA encoder weights; used to warm-start generators that output de novo backbones, motif-scaffolded backbones and conformational ensembles
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Geometric pretraining before generative finetuning, de novo backbone generation, zero-shot motif scaffolding, conformational-ensemble modelling including GPCRs
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from arXiv API (v3 2026-10-18), bioRxiv API (v1-v3) and v3 full text, ICLR 2026 poster page, GitHub API (MIT, not a fork), HF model and dataset APIs (ungated, MIT label, two checkpoints) and the ATLAS download page (CC BY-NC 4.0). noncommercial=true because the redistributed Phase II data derives from CC BY-NC ATLAS despite its MIT label; whether that term reaches the RigidSSL-MD weights is unsettled. catalog_upserts.name: LIMBER
catalog_upserts.description: Hybrid RNA language model that interleaves bidirectional Transformer attention with Mamba selective state-space layers in a repeating Transformer-Transformer-Mamba pattern, pretrained by masked language modelling on about 40.5 million RNAcentral sequences. Three headline checkpoints (91.7M, 303.6M and 664.3M parameters) are released together with the paper's size-, data- and budget-scaling panel and size-matched pure-Transformer and pure-Mamba controls.
catalog_upserts.status: Public code and ungated Hugging Face weights, but no licence is stated for either: the repository has no LICENSE file and the hub card declares no licence, so all rights are reserved by default. Pretraining sequences are not redistributed; no API.

catalog_upserts.use_cases: RNA representation learning, secondary-structure prediction, non-coding RNA family classification, zero-shot mutational-fitness scoring, architecture and scaling studies using the released control checkpoints

catalog_upserts.name: SynCodonLM
catalog_upserts.description: Codon language model (DeBERTa-v2 encoder, 12 layers, hidden size 768) from Boehringer Ingelheim, pretrained with synonymous-codon-constrained masking: logits of non-synonymous codons are masked so that codon-usage patterns are learned apart from protein-level semantics. Species token types supply host context (a V2 variant without token types is also released), and the checkpoints give codon-level and mean-pooled embeddings for downstream coding-sequence models.

catalog_upserts.name: ProtRNA
catalog_upserts.description: RNA language model built by cross-modality transfer learning from the protein language model ESM-2: the protein model is adapted to RNA sequences so that information learned on proteins can be reused for low-resource RNA data, and the authors report comparable or better downstream performance with 1/8 the trainable parameters and 1/6 the training data of their primary reference RNA language model. The released checkpoint produces nucleotide-level embeddings, and trained prediction heads for secondary structure, protein-RNA binding (17 RBPs, HeLa) and 5' UTR mean ribosome load are published alongside it.

catalog_upserts.io: RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide embeddings; with released heads -> secondary-structure, RNA-protein binding and 5' UTR mean-ribosome-load predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: RNA representation learning on scarce RNA data, secondary-structure prediction, protein-RNA interaction prediction, mean-ribosome-load prediction, cross-modality transfer studies
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 from Crossref, the bioRxiv API and abstract page (which links the GitHub repository), the GitHub API (Apache-2.0 LICENSE; pretrained.py downloads from zenodo.org/records/14795554) and the Zenodo API (file listing, CC BY 4.0, open, creators matching the paper authors). Limits: the Cell Systems full text is paywalled and was not read, so model size and training-data figures are not restated beyond the abstract; the version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14795554 is registered at DataCite but its Zenodo redirect returned 404 on 2026-11-06, so the record is linked directly; a newer Zenodo version v2.1 (record 14840194) exists with an identical ProtRNA_pretrained.h5 checksum; code (Apache-2.0) and Zenodo content (CC BY 4.0) are two different grants, and upstream terms of repackaged benchmark data were not checked; the implementation is TensorFlow and the repository was last pushed 2025-05-06. Nothing was downloaded or executed and reported task performance is author-reported.

catalog_upserts.name: RESM
catalog_upserts.description: RNA language model trained by mapping RNA sequences onto pseudo-protein sequences so that pretraining transfers from the protein language model ESM-2. Two checkpoints (about 150M and 650M parameters) are released; the authors report zero-shot and fine-tuned gains over existing RNA language models on classification, secondary structure, RNA-RNA interaction and translation-related tasks, and use beyond the 1,024-nucleotide training length, although training used non-coding RNA only.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: MIT code (LICENSE.txt); checkpoints and datasets in an open, ungated CC BY 4.0 Zenodo record, distributed as two large archives (ckpt.zip about 4 GB, data.zip about 6.4 GB); the bundled datasets derive from third-party sources whose own terms were not re-checked. No API. The bioRxiv article text is CC BY-NC-ND, which covers the article, not the model.
catalog_upserts.io: RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide embeddings and attention maps (inputs for base-pairing); after fine-tuning -> secondary structure, RNA-RNA interaction, ribosome-loading and expression predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: RNA representation learning, secondary-structure prediction for long RNAs, RNA-RNA interaction prediction, mRNA ribosome-loading and expression prediction, zero-shot RNA sequence classification
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from the bioRxiv API, the GitHub API (MIT LICENSE.txt, README, resm_inference.py) and the Zenodo API (file listing, cc-by-4.0, open, creator = first author, single version). Limits: preprint only (v1, 2025-08-10), no journal version; checkpoint archive contents not listed individually (Zenodo zip preview and landing pages blocked this client; nothing downloaded); repository last pushed 2025-08-11; the 81.3% improvement and >1000-fold speedup are author-reported.

catalog_upserts.name: mRNA-LM
catalog_upserts.description: Full-length mRNA language model from Sanofi built from three self-supervised BERT-style component models, one each for the 5' UTR (5UTRBERT), the coding sequence (CodonBERT, catalogued separately) and the 3' UTR (3UTRBERT, not the Yang et al. 3UTRBERT), pretrained on over 10 million mRNA sequences from multiple species. For a given task, a CLIP-style module joins the three segment embeddings into one full-length representation and is fine-tuned with LoRA; the paper evaluates mRNA half-life, translation rate, transcript expression and protein expression. Only the three component checkpoints are released, not a pretrained joint model or fine-tuned task heads.
catalog_upserts.status: Non-commercial. Code is public on GitHub under a custom Sanofi non-commercial notice (academic research and non-commercial use only, granted to people from academic or non-profit organisations; all other rights reserved), and a separate artifact notice applies the same terms to the trained weights. The three pretrained component checkpoints (about 955-961 MB zip archives each) download from a Sanofi CDN without an account or gating; no model hub repository, no checksums, no API. No pretrained joint model or fine-tuned task heads are released. The Zenodo code snapshot is labelled CC BY 4.0, which conflicts with the repository notices.
catalog_upserts.io: 5' UTR, coding-sequence and 3' UTR sequences -> per-segment embeddings from the three pretrained encoders; after task fine-tuning of the CLIP joint module and head -> full-length mRNA property predictions (half-life, translation rate, transcript or protein expression)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Full-length mRNA representation learning, prediction of mRNA stability, translation and expression, ranking candidate mRNA sequences (for example for vaccine design)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from Crossref, the Europe PMC full-text XML and the PMC page, the GitHub API (both licence notices read in full, README, FullModel.py, data listing), one-byte range requests against all three CDN archives (HTTP 206, nothing downloaded) and the Zenodo API. Limits: no pretrained joint checkpoint exists, so the reusable artifacts are the three component encoders; CodonBERT overlaps bfm-codonbert; the Zenodo snapshot comes from the first author's fork and is labelled CC BY 4.0 against the repository's non-commercial notices; weights sit on a vendor CDN with no checksum or retention statement; FullModel.py hard-codes local model paths. Archive contents were not listed and performance claims are author-reported.

catalog_upserts.name: RiboGRAM
catalog_upserts.description: Self-supervised non-coding RNA language model: a 12-layer encoder that combines parallel multi-scale convolutions (1-9 nt kernels) with rotary self-attention, pretrained by masked nucleotide reconstruction on about 40 million non-redundant ncRNA sequences from RNAcentral, Rfam and Ensembl. The authors motivate it with multi-scale motif usage and 5'-to-3' positional gradients that set ncRNAs apart from coding sequences across nine organisms. They report that its embeddings organise ncRNA families and recover base pairing better than their own CDS- and mRNA-pretrained control models, and that it supports RNA-protein, RNA-RNA and RNA-chromatin interaction prediction. The paper also describes RiboGRAM-3D, an MSA-free diffusion model for tertiary structures of short RNAs. All results are author-reported.
catalog_upserts.status: Code, the pretrained RiboGRAM checkpoint (about 3.4 GB), ncRNA classification heads, interaction checkpoints and the datasets are openly downloadable from a Zenodo record of four archives (about 53.4 GB). The base checkpoint and heads are also included in the source-code archive. The record is labelled CC BY 4.0, but its description states that no single project-level licence is specified and that software, checkpoints and datasets may carry different terms. The code package has no licence file, and bundled third-party datasets keep their own terms. The RiboGRAM-3D package needs a separate STAR RNA backbone checkpoint that is not included. The project portal marks its downloads as open to reviewers only, its web server requires a login, and the cited Code Ocean capsule was not reachable. There is no GitHub repository or model hub card.
catalog_upserts.io: Non-coding RNA sequence -> per-nucleotide and sequence embeddings and attention maps; with the released heads -> 13-category and 88-family ncRNA labels, and RNA-protein, RNA-RNA and RNA-chromatin interaction scores; RiboGRAM-3D (requires an external backbone checkpoint not in the release) -> MSA-free tertiary structures of short RNAs
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Non-coding RNA representation learning, ncRNA category and family classification, RNA-protein, RNA-RNA and RNA-chromatin interaction prediction, attention-based base-pair analysis, MSA-free tertiary modelling of short RNAs (RiboGRAM-3D)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified on 2026-11-06 from the bioRxiv API, the preprint's JATS full text, the Zenodo API record and version list, and the project portal. Model files were confirmed by reading only the zip central directory (a 64 KB range read, no weights downloaded): RiboGRAM.pkl, PLM-CDS/PLM-mRNA control checkpoints, two ncRNA heads and four interaction checkpoints. Limits: (1) the Zenodo licence field (CC BY 4.0) conflicts with the record's own statement that no project-level licence is specified, and the code package has no licence file; (2) the RiboGRAM-3D release needs a separate STAR backbone checkpoint, which the paper does not mention (it describes a frozen RiboGRAM encoder); (3) the Zenodo landing page and DOI return 403 to automated clients; (4) the portal downloads are reviewer-only and the web server requires a login; (5) Code Ocean returned 403; (6) single preprint version, no journal version. Nothing was executed, and all performance claims are author-reported.

catalog_upserts.name: CellNet
catalog_upserts.description: Cross-species single-cell transcriptome foundation model that renders each cell as an image combining DNA-derived gene identities with measured expression and encodes it with a ViT-B/16 backbone trained by multi-view JEPA objectives; pretrained on about 231 million cell profiles from 40 species covering over one million genes.
catalog_upserts.status: Apache-2.0 code (README and NOTICE scope the licence to code); pretrained weights (weights/cellnet.pt, about 946 MB, and projector.pt) are public and ungated via Git LFS in the same GitHub repository with no stated weight licence (all rights reserved by default); the encoder is a DINOv3 ViT-B/16 base model and the repository supports DINOv3 initialisation, but neither paper nor repository states whether the released checkpoint was initialised from DINOv3 weights (governed by the DINOv3 License); pretraining Image Atlas on Baidu Netdisk with a published extraction code, source datasets keep their original terms (dataset card: per-source licence verification pending); no API
catalog_upserts.io: scRNA-seq expression (h5ad) mapped onto species-specific gene-image layouts -> cell embeddings, expression predictions for measured and unmeasured genes, gene representations
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Cross-species cell representation and annotation, recognition of rare and condition-associated cell states, expression inference beyond measured gene panels, association of poorly characterised non-coding RNAs with known programmes
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Discovery (single-cell lane) 2026-11-06. arXiv v1 15 Oct 2026, v2 2 Nov 2026; no venue. Full text (HTML) read for code availability; the paper links only the website, which links the repo. weights/cellnet.pt (about 946 MB) is a Git LFS object; the media URL answered a HEAD request with the expected size; not downloaded or run. Terms limit: Apache-2.0 is stated for code; no separate licence covers the weights. The encoder is the DINOv3 ViT-B/16 architecture and the training guide supports DINOv3 initialisation (DINOv3 License, restricted end uses, derivatives bound by its terms); whether the released checkpoint derives from DINOv3 weights is not stated. Data terms file on the website not read. Not to be confused with the older CellNet network-biology platform for cell-fate engineering (different tool; neither is in the catalog). Adversarial verification 2026-11-06: arXiv API, full text, website, repo contents, LFS pointers and media HEAD re-fetched; status reworded so weights read as unlicensed (all rights reserved) and data terms as pending per-source verification. Paper S.2.9 gives peak LR 2e-5 and 14 days of training but no initialisation statement.

catalog_upserts.name: ChromFound
catalog_upserts.description: Foundation model for single-cell chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq) that combines windowed self-attention and Mamba blocks with genome-aware tokenization of open chromatin regions; pretrained on 1.97 million human cells from 30 tissues and 6 disease conditions.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: Apache-2.0 code on GitHub; ungated Apache-2.0 pretrained checkpoint on Hugging Face (first author's account, linked from the official README; Google Drive mirror also linked). Released scripts cover cell embedding and cell-type annotation. Requires CUDA GPUs with FlashAttention. No API
catalog_upserts.io: Human scATAC-seq profiles (open chromatin regions with hg38 positions) -> zero-shot cell embeddings; after fine-tuning: cell-type labels and gene-expression predictions from chromatin accessibility
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot scATAC cell representation and clustering, cell-type annotation, cross-omics prediction (accessibility to expression), enhancer-gene link and enhancer-perturbation response prediction (K562 demonstration in the paper)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older miss found in the 2026-11-06 single-cell lane. arXiv v1 May 2025, v3 26 Oct 2025; NeurIPS 2025 poster per OpenReview venue field. The paper's repository URL (JohnsonKlose/ChromFound) redirects to SAIS-LifeScience/ChromFound. The HF repo is under the personal account YifengJiao (first author) and is linked from the official README. checkpoints/model.pt is about 1.9 MB (embedding dim 128, 4 encoder layers, matching the paper); seen in the file listing, not downloaded or run. Limit: the shipped chromfd_pretrain.yaml lists only PBMC-benchmark (GSE194028) training files and lr 1e-4 versus the paper's 5e-5, so it is not confirmed that model.pt is the full 1.97M-cell pretraining checkpoint. No released code for the cross-omics or enhancer-gene tasks was seen.

catalog_upserts.name: BMFM-RNA
catalog_upserts.description: IBM Research family of single-cell transcriptomic foundation models built with the open biomed-multi-omic framework. Released checkpoints: BERT 110M (2025; MLM, MLM with read-depth-aware downsampling, whole-cell expression decoding (WCED), and multitask fine-tuned variants) and Llama-style 32M/47M (2026; MLM or WCED pretraining combined with multitask training that includes a Cell Ontology hierarchical cell-type loss).
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: Apache-2.0 code; six ungated Apache-2.0 Hugging Face checkpoints (ibm-research/biomed.rna.*), plus vLLM-format copies of the two Llama checkpoints; no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: scRNA-seq AnnData (raw counts, gene symbols) -> cell embeddings; multitask checkpoints also give cell-type/tissue predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot cell embeddings and batch integration, linear-probe and Cell Ontology hierarchical zero-shot cell-type annotation, fine-tuned cell-type classification, drug mechanism-of-action linear probing from embeddings; the framework also supports further fine-tuning (including perturbation tasks, not benchmarked in the paper)
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Older miss found in the 2026-11-06 single-cell lane; adversarially reviewed. arXiv v1 2025-06-17, v2 2026-03-26 (title changed); preprint, not peer reviewed. Hub API checked for all 8 ibm-research/biomed.rna.* repos (6 checkpoints + 2 vLLM-format copies; all ungated, apache-2.0, cite arXiv 2506.14861); 3 cards read in full; repo README lists the six checkpoints. Shares the biomed-multi-omic repository with BMFM-DNA (bfm-bmfm-dna) but is a separate RNA model family. Pretraining corpus sizes not independently checked; no weights downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: CONCH-Z
catalog_upserts.description: Pathology vision-language model from the Mahmood Lab that keeps the CONCH v1.5 ViT-L/16 vision encoder and image projection frozen and realigns its 110M-parameter CoCa text encoder to about 335,000 clinical pathology reports using LIMIT (Locked Image Multiple Instance PreTraining), so patch embeddings can be compared directly with free-text class descriptions for zero-shot classification.
catalog_upserts.status: Gated Hugging Face weights and inference code (access form; Hugging Face primary email must match an institutional email, personal-domain requests denied) under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, non-commercial academic research only, no redistribution; contrastive encoders only, no caption decoder. The GitHub repository has no licence file and currently contains only a README; LIMIT training code is announced but not released. Non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route
catalog_upserts.io: H&E image patch (448 x 448) and/or text prompt (up to 127 tokens) -> 768-d L2-normalised image and text embeddings in a shared space; zero-shot class probabilities; precomputed CONCH v1.5 patch features can be projected into the same space
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot patch-level tissue and tumour classification from text prompts, zero-shot tumour detection and slide-level cancer subtyping, adding text-queryable zero-shot classification to existing CONCH v1.5 feature pipelines
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 from the arXiv abstract and HTML full text, the GitHub repository and licence API, the hub API file listing and the rendered model card (raw card and config are behind the gate). Limits: weights and bundled inference code are gated with institutional-email vetting under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; the GitHub repository has no licence and no code; training code is announced but not released; it is a CONCH v1.5 derivative in which only the text tower was trained (HF base_model: MahmoodLab/conchv1_5), so curators may prefer to file it as CONCH family. Distinct from bfm-conch (CONCH v1) and bfm-titan. Weights were not downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: spaGFM
catalog_upserts.description: Graph foundation model for image-based spatial transcriptomics that serialises cellular neighbourhoods with random walks and learns by self-supervised neighbourhood reconstruction instead of message passing; pretrained on 43.9 million cells from 132 human and mouse Xenium, CosMx and MERSCOPE samples, released as 36M- and 317M-parameter human and mouse checkpoints.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights: MIT code (inference, fine-tuning and pretraining scripts); four ungated MIT-labelled checkpoints (human/mouse, 36M/317M) on Hugging Face; inference also needs the frozen scGPT human checkpoint bundled in the same hub repo (upstream scGPT terms), which ships with CosMx demo data under the vendor's own terms; 3M/15M variants in the paper are not released
catalog_upserts.io: Image-based spatial transcriptomics (per-cell expression embedded with a frozen scGPT human checkpoint, plus a Delaunay cell graph from spatial coordinates; neighbourhoods serialised by random walks) -> cell-level and neighbourhood-level embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot cell-type and niche label transfer across samples; tissue-structure detection (e.g. tertiary lymphoid structures) across cohorts and platforms; cell-level perturbation-response analysis in spatial CRISPR (Perturb-FISH) data; glomerular organisation analysis in diabetic kidney disease
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 against the Research Square preprint full text, whose Code availability names github.com/yzhong36/spaGFM as the official repository. Also checked: Crossref metadata, the GitHub repository and its licence API, the hub API file listing and the hub owner profile (full name Yu Zhong, the preprint's second author). The repo README links the hub weights. Limits: the preprint is not peer-reviewed. The hub card has only a licence field. Inference depends on a bundled frozen scGPT human checkpoint whose checkpoint-specific terms were not checked, and the bundled CosMx demo data keep vendor terms. Weights were not downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: DeepCellMorpho
catalog_upserts.description: Self-supervised image encoders for Cell Painting morphological profiling from Johnson & Johnson (MAE ViT-B/16, iTPN HiViT-B/16, DINO ViT-B/16 and DINOv2 variants), pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations of JUMP-CP (119,876 compounds, about 1.77 million images) without cell segmentation. DINO and DINOv2 models outperformed CellProfiler features on replicate and mechanism-of-action retrieval and transferred to unseen cell types.

catalog_upserts.status: Apache 2.0 code (per CODE LICENSE file; GitHub detects no SPDX licence); eight ungated pretrained checkpoints in the repository via Git LFS and precomputed embeddings (repository and Zenodo) under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial); non-commercial terms apply to at least one artifact or access route
