catalog_upserts.use_cases: Image-based phenotypic profiling, compound replicate retrieval, mechanism-of-action retrieval, cross-cell-type transfer for drug-discovery screens
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified 2026-11-06 from the open-access Nature Methods article (Data and Code availability statements name the J&J repository and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the pretrained models), Crossref, the GitHub repository (README, licence files, git tree), the Git LFS batch API (download action returned for all eight checkpoints, 178 MB to 1.75 GB) and the Zenodo embeddings record (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). The README licence sentence names both 'CC BY-NC 4.0' and 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0'; the licence file and article say BY-NC-SA. Limits: weights were not downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: QuiltNet
catalog_upserts.description: Histopathology vision-language model obtained by fine-tuning a pre-trained OpenAI CLIP model on Quilt-1M, about one million histopathology image-text pairs largely curated from educational YouTube videos (plus Twitter, research papers and web sources). Released as three checkpoints: ViT-B/32 and ViT-B/16 with GPT-2-style 77-token text encoders, and ViT-B/16 with a PubMedBERT text encoder (QuiltNet-B-16-PMB).
catalog_upserts.status: MIT code and MIT-labelled ungated weights (three checkpoints) on Hugging Face; the model cards (inherited from OpenAI CLIP) put any deployed use, commercial or not, out of scope; the Quilt-1M training data are released only after agreeing to research-use terms
catalog_upserts.io: Histopathology image and/or text -> aligned CLIP-style image and text embeddings; zero-shot classification and image-text retrieval
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Zero-shot tissue classification, linear probing, cross-modal image-text retrieval, starting checkpoint for fine-tuning on pathology image tasks
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Catalog-gap addition, not a release in the November window. Verified 2026-11-06 from the arXiv abstract and HTML, DataCite, the GitHub README and licence API, the hub API listings for all three checkpoints, the B-32 and B-16 cards, and the Zenodo record API. Code and weights are MIT and ungated. noncommercial=true because the Quilt-1M data require a research-use commitment (Zenodo access 'restricted') and the cards exclude any deployed use; the weight licence itself is permissive. NeurIPS 2023 (oral) is stated in the authors' README and was not checked against the proceedings. The B-32 hub repo also holds undocumented extra checkpoint files (dino_checkpoint, cyto_histo, all_inclusive). Nothing downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: CIFM (Cell Interaction Foundation Model)
catalog_upserts.description: Caltech (Thomson lab) spatial-transcriptomics foundation model. It is a geometric graph neural network, trained self-supervised to infer each cell's gene expression from its spatial microenvironment by masked-transcriptome prediction. The released checkpoint has 100M parameters and was trained on about 23 million cells from 10x Visium and Xenium data. A 2026 preprint from the same group describes an extended CIFM. That version is retrained on a curated corpus at 100M to 4B parameters and used as a generative 'virtual tissue' for in silico perturbation design. Its model and code are available only on request.
catalog_upserts.status: Public, ungated 100M checkpoint on Hugging Face, with model code, a tutorial notebook and an example AnnData file. It is tagged MIT in the card metadata only (no LICENSE file). The GitHub repository is README-only with no licence. Code for the 2026 preprint is available only on request, and its 400M, 1B and 4B models are not released.
catalog_upserts.io: Spatial transcriptomics (cells with coordinates and expression, AnnData) -> cell-microenvironment embeddings; predicted expression of cells at target locations; iterative (autoregressive) simulation of tissue responses
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Microenvironment embedding, spatial gene-expression prediction and imputation, sample-condition classification by linear probing, in silico simulation of tissue responses to perturbations such as T-cell infiltration
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Checked 2026-11-06 via the bioRxiv API and full texts, the Hugging Face API and file tree, and the GitHub API. Neither preprint is peer reviewed. The 2025 preprint itself links huggingface.co/ynyou/CIFM. MIT appears only as a hub-card licence tag: there is no LICENSE file, and the GitHub repo declares no licence. The 2026 preprint does not link the hub checkpoint and offers code on request. Its corpus differs from the 2025 one (18,000 vs 32,000 genes; 56 samples / 16 tissue types vs ~100 slides), and it states both that simulations used the 100M configuration and that a 1B model was selected as the operating point. Its 400M-4B models are not released. Hub metadata reports 142M stored parameters for the nominal 100M model. The hub repo includes an example adata.h5ad whose source is not stated. Paper licences (CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-ND) cover the preprint text only. Hub card last modified 2025-02-12. Nothing downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: TERRA
catalog_upserts.description: Spatial transcriptomics foundation model from the Lotfollahi lab: a transformer pretrained with a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) on HST-Corpus-112M (about 112 million human cells from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics) that gives zero-shot gene-, cell- and neighbourhood-level embeddings and supports spatial in silico perturbation. TERRA-112M uses the full corpus; TERRA-96M holds out 215 sections for benchmarking.
catalog_upserts.status: BSD-3-Clause code (GitHub, PyPI terra-st); ungated Hugging Face weights (TERRA-112M, TERRA-96M) under CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial); pretraining corpus not released (a subset is promised upon publication); preprint not peer reviewed.
catalog_upserts.io: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (single-cell gene expression with spatial coordinates, targeted gene panels) -> gene, cell and neighbourhood embeddings; in silico perturbation predictions (sequencing-based data such as Visium via LoRA fine-tuning)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Niche and cell-type identification, batch-integrated spatial atlasing, cross-tissue niche (archetype) mapping, spatial gene-pair scoring, in silico gene knockout
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint (not peer reviewed); CC-BY-NC-4.0 weights; repo README and hub cards still cite the manuscript as in preparation (link runs paper -> repo/hub only); pretraining corpus subset promised upon publication.

catalog_upserts.name: XMAG
catalog_upserts.description: Lightweight pathology patch encoder from Ohio State University: an 86M-parameter DINOv2 ViT-B/14 student that works at 5x magnification, distilled with global and local feature alignment from a frozen UNI2 (ViT-H) teacher seeing the matching 20x region, so slides need about 11 times fewer patches; trained on 3.49 million 5x patches from 6,703 public TCGA slides across 16 cancer types.
catalog_upserts.status: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 code (GitHub LICENSE); ungated Hugging Face weights (student EMA backbone only, custom remote code) whose card licence section states PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 in wording addressed to 'code' (no hub licence field); the README also links a Google Drive checkpoint. Distilled from UNI2-h, whose CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms bar commercial use of models trained on its outputs without prior approval. Training slides are public TCGA.
catalog_upserts.io: H&E patches (224 x 224 at 5x / ~2 um mpp) -> 768-dimensional CLS and patch embeddings
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Fast whole-slide feature extraction at low magnification; slide-level cancer classification and subtyping via MIL; patch-level tissue phenotyping; tumour segmentation; resource-constrained pathology pipelines
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from arXiv v4 PDF (Code Availability names the GitHub repo), Crossref, GitHub repo/LICENSE/README, hub API file listing and card, and the UNI2-h public card. The PolyForm NC statement on repo and card is worded for 'code' and the hub has no licence field; read as covering the weights. Teacher UNI2-h terms (CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0) bar commercial use of models trained on its outputs; whether its ND clause permits public release of the student was not settled (as for DistillPath). arXiv abstract metadata says six tasks, v4 full text seven. No weights downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: OMNI
catalog_upserts.description: Family of four pathology tile encoders (7.3M to 330M parameters) distilled at once from ten pathology and vision foundation models on 10M tiles from 10k TCGA slides, learning one token per teacher with a structured attention mask, mixture-of-experts layers and a contrastive loss; the default embedding averages the ten teacher-specific tokens.
catalog_upserts.status: CC BY-NC 4.0 ungated weights for four sizes on Hugging Face, with inference code in the hub repos; GitHub training/evaluation code has no licence (all rights reserved). Teachers include UNI2-h and Virchow2, both gated under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; whether their terms permit distributing distilled students was not settled.
catalog_upserts.io: H&E image tiles (224 x 224) -> averaged tile embedding, ten teacher-specific tokens and patch tokens
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Efficient tile feature extraction for whole-slide pipelines; tile-level classification; slide-level MIL tasks
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Adversarially re-verified 2026-11-06 from the arXiv API, abstract and HTML full text, GitHub README and API (licence null), project pages and hub APIs/file listings for all four sizes. NeurIPS 2026 acceptance is stated in the arXiv comment and model cards; proceedings not checked. GitHub code has no licence. Teacher terms (UNI2-h and Virchow2 are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and gated; their card text was not readable) for distilled students were not settled, as for DistillPath. Released patch-feature datasets were not checked. No weights downloaded or run.

catalog_upserts.name: K-Fold
catalog_upserts.description: MSA-free generative co-folding model from KAIST (with HITS) that assembles independently predicted unbound (apo) component structures into a bound complex through a diffusion bridge, aimed at binding-induced conformational states. Supports proteins, DNA, RNA, small molecules and residue modifications. The preprint evaluates it on FoldBench interface types, antibody-antigen (FoldBench, PXM-2025), molecular-glue (MGBench), kinase and GPCR state sets.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0): GitHub code and PyPI package; K-Fold weights and supporting assets (TriProRep structure encoder, RNA sequence encoder, CCD) ungated on Hugging Face. Also requires the pretrained AtlasLM protein-sequence encoder and AtlasFold (default apo generation), ungated under MIT on the developer's Hugging Face account.

catalog_upserts.name: GenCDR
catalog_upserts.description: Family of decoder-only (LLaMA-architecture) antibody language models from AstraZeneca that read all four frameworks as a conditioning prompt and generate CDR1-CDR3 jointly as a variable-length response, which keeps framework and CDR likelihoods separable for scoring and reward-based alignment. IgGenCDR is pretrained on about 254 million unpaired human OAS sequences; p-IgGenCDR (about 1.8 million paired OAS sequences) and NanoGenCDR (about 6.5 million INDI VHH sequences) are fine-tuned from it.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (Apache-2.0): three checkpoints published as GitHub release assets and downloaded automatically by the package on first use; no gating, no API
catalog_upserts.io: Antibody framework prompt (FR1-FR4 for a heavy, light or paired chain, or a VHH framework) -> jointly generated variable-length CDR1/CDR2/CDR3 sequences, with separable framework and CDR likelihoods for scoring
catalog_upserts.use_cases: De novo CDR design and CDR grafting onto a chosen framework, nanobody CDR generation, paired heavy-light CDR design, likelihood-based scoring of designs, and reward-weighted DPO alignment against binding, expression or developability objectives
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06; the October artifact blocker is cleared. Weights were released on 2026-10-25 as release v1.0.0 assets (iggencdr.zip 93,772,233 bytes, nanogencdr.zip 93,813,958 bytes, p-iggencdr.zip 93,767,720 bytes) with the release body and README both stating Apache-2.0; repository licence Apache-2.0 per the GitHub API. Assets were confirmed by the releases API listing and not downloaded, so checkpoint contents were not inspected and nothing was run. Primary source is a bioRxiv preprint (v1 2026-09-10, CC BY), not peer reviewed; Crossref shows no journal version. Reported results, including the alignment rounds against co-folding and developability objectives, are author-reported in silico. Name caution: p-IgGenCDR is part of this family and is distinct from p-IgGen (bfm-p-iggen, OPIG/AstraZeneca paired antibody generator).

catalog_upserts.name: CaLM (Codon adaptation Language Model)
catalog_upserts.description: 86-million-parameter language model trained on about 9 million non-redundant coding DNA (cDNA) sequences from the European Nucleotide Archive, using codons instead of amino acids as tokens; its embeddings serve as protein representations and outperformed comparable protein language models on tasks such as species recognition, protein and transcript abundance and melting-point prediction.
catalog_upserts.status: BSD-3-Clause code; ungated pretrained weights (calm_weights.pkl, Python pickle, about 343 MB) and training/held-out sets served from the authors' OPIG server and linked in the paper, with no licence stated for weights or data (all rights reserved by default); no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Coding DNA sequence -> codon-level and sequence embeddings for downstream property predictors
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Protein and transcript abundance prediction, species recognition, melting-point estimation, protein engineering from coding sequences, codon-aware sequence representation
catalog_upserts.audit_note: The paper's Data availability section links the OPIG weight URL that the package hard-codes, so the weights come from the authors. That URL returned 403 on 2026-10-10 and 200 on 2026-11-06 (HEAD: 343,092,322 bytes, last-modified 2023-05-19). Availability depends on one university server; the package requests it over http, which redirects to https, and loads it with pickle.load. BSD-3-Clause covers the repository code only. No licence is stated for the weights or the training/held-out data. The bioRxiv preprint text is CC BY-NC (article licence, not a model artifact); the journal article is CC BY 4.0. Repository inactive since 2024-10. Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Zatom-2
catalog_upserts.description: Multiscale Transformer (about 70M-270M parameters) trained with conditional flow matching and multitask-pretrained on about five million OMol25 molecular and OMat24 materials structures, covering 3D generation with optional force conditioning, structure prediction and auxiliary energy and force prediction; finetuning transfers it to low-data protein backbone generation. Successor of Zatom-1.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code (LBNL modified-BSD, also on PyPI); public ungated paper checkpoints on the authors' Hugging Face repo (licence MIT in card metadata only, no licence file); training data third-party (OMol25 via Meta's gated hub card, OMat24; both CC BY 4.0 per paper); third-party evaluation models keep their own, partly gated terms; no hosted API
catalog_upserts.io: Noise, optionally with a force-regime condition -> 3D molecules, crystals (atom types, coordinates, lattice) or protein backbones; atom types -> 3D geometry (and lattice for crystals) by structure prediction; 3D atomistic structure -> energy, force and, via finetuned heads, property predictions
catalog_upserts.use_cases: 3D small-molecule and crystal generation, force-conditioned sampling, molecular and crystal structure prediction, property prediction via finetuning, low-data protein backbone generation via transfer learning; energy/force prediction as an auxiliary task, not a replacement for specialised MLIPs
catalog_upserts.audit_note: arXiv preprint (v2, 2026-10-10), not peer reviewed. The code licence is LBNL modified-BSD (root and models/zatom2 LICENSE.md, PyPI). The weight licence is only the MIT tag in the HF card YAML; the HF repo has no LICENSE file. The HF repo holds 28 checkpoints named by paper table/figure; the CLI default is the large (about 270M) joint-property, force-conditioned model. The repo's release-status doc says MP20 structure-prediction and GEOM-Drugs checkpoints are not released. Paper and repo give OMol25/OMat24 as CC BY 4.0; the upstream OMol25 hub card is manually gated. Energy/force heads are auxiliary, and the authors do not aim to match specialised MLIPs. The protein result is one small SCOPe transfer experiment. Biology link as for Zatom-1 (drug-like molecules, protein-domain finetuning). Weights not downloaded or executed.

catalog_upserts.name: Ares
catalog_upserts.description: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts masked protein language model family (~4.2B parameters) pretrained from scratch on UniRef50, comparing loss-free Soft-MoE and Expert-Choice routing for bidirectional protein encoders. Five pretrained checkpoints are released (the soft-routing ones are recommended; expert-choice ones are weaker or unevaluated) together with training, evaluation and MoE interpretability tooling.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights (MIT code; five ungated MIT checkpoints on Hugging Face; requires installing the ares package from GitHub)
catalog_upserts.io: Protein sequence -> per-residue and pooled embeddings, masked-residue logits (zero-shot variant scoring)
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Protein representation learning and fine-tuning for property prediction, zero-shot variant-effect scoring (ProteinGym), study of MoE routing and expert specialization in protein encoders
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Primary report is a single-author workshop paper; only the ICML abstract page was readable (OpenReview forum shows a browser challenge, API and PDF return 403), so scale and UniRef50 corpus rest on the official README and model cards; README/card call the citation not final. Training corpus is a third-party HF UniRef50 copy without licence metadata (not redistributed). Expert-choice router flagged by the author as not faithful to the original formulation.

catalog_upserts.name: AtomWeaver
catalog_upserts.description: Multi-component flow-matching inverse-folding model from ProteinQure that generates peptide side chains as atom clouds in 3D for a fixed peptide backbone bound to a target protein, then reads off residue identity at decode time by geometric matching against a reference library of canonical and non-canonical amino acids. Three read-out vocabularies ship (20, 300 and 450 residue classes; the 450-class set is not a superset of the 300-class one). Adding a new non-canonical residue requires reference rotamers plus a refit of the small CPU read-out head, not retraining of the model weights.
catalog_upserts.status: AGPL-3.0 code (LICENSE-CODE); atomweaver.pt weights (201,811,099 bytes, ~192 MiB) and the read-out training clouds (readout_train_clouds.npz) on the v1.0.0 GitHub release (2026-10-16) under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-WEIGHTS), ungated, no account needed; reference libraries and read-out heads bundled in the repository under the repository terms; no hosted API; historical research configurations and model-training APIs not maintained
catalog_upserts.io: Peptide backbone + target protein structure (PDB) -> designed peptide sequences including non-canonical residues (FASTA with bracketed CCD codes, CSV with per-position top-3 probabilities, JSON read-out distributions) and side-chain atom-cloud PDBs
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Target-conditioned fixed-backbone peptide design with non-canonical amino acids, narrowing or extending the read-out vocabulary by refitting the read-out head, peptide therapeutic lead design
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Preprint v1 (2026-09-28, CC BY) not peer reviewed; comparative performance claims in the preprint not independently assessed. Code is AGPL-3.0, so networked services built on it inherit copyleft; weights are CC BY 4.0. Scope is fixed-backbone peptide inverse folding, admitted on the same precedent as the displayed ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN/ESM-IF1 records, not as a structure predictor; if that precedent is narrowed, this record falls with them. Weight file existence and ungated access checked from release metadata and a 1-byte range request; weights were not downloaded or executed, so the checkpoint contents and reproducibility of the reported results are unverified.

catalog_upserts.name: BacPT
catalog_upserts.description: Bacterial proteome foundation model that contextualizes ESM2 protein embeddings by the order of proteins in a genome, trained self-supervised (masked embedding reconstruction) on about 33,000 complete RefSeq bacterial genomes. Two checkpoints (BacPT-small, RoBERTa backbone, about 51M parameters; BacPT-large, RoFormer backbone, about 74M parameters) produce contextual gene embeddings for downstream functional, trait and ecological prediction.
catalog_upserts.status: Open code + weights, ungated: MIT code (GitHub LICENSE) and two public Hugging Face checkpoints with their own MIT LICENSE file, downloadable without an account. Inference fetches ESM2 (facebookresearch/esm, MIT) via PyTorch Hub on first use. No API/server; training corpus not released (genomes from NCBI RefSeq). Preprint text is CC BY-NC 4.0 (article only, not the model).
catalog_upserts.io: Protein FASTA already ordered by genomic position (up to 5,000 proteins; proteins over 2,250 aa omitted; ESM2 embeddings computed internally) -> contextual per-protein embeddings (480-d) and reconstructed ESM2 vectors
catalog_upserts.use_cases: Genome-context-aware gene representations for bacteria; enzyme activity, biosynthetic gene cluster and metabolic trait prediction; gene interaction analysis; prediction of microbial ecological interaction outcomes
catalog_upserts.audit_note: Verified from primary sources on 2026-11-06 (adversarial review). The preprint's Code availability (v1 and v2) names github.com/palsetuf/BacPT; that MIT repository (copyright Palash Sethi, Lucas A. Pereira, Juannan Zhou, matching the preprint authors) links both Hugging Face checkpoints under the palsetuf account (Palash Sethi, University of Florida org), whose own LICENSE is MIT. Hub listings and release manifests (parameter counts, SHA-256) were inspected; nothing was downloaded or executed. Limits: preprint only (v2, not peer-reviewed); HF cards do not yet carry the citation; input requires proteins already in genomic order; not validated outside bacteria; ESM2 dependency fetched from upstream at run time; benchmarks author-reported. Modality protein follows the ProteomeLM precedent; gLM is catalogued as dna - curator may align.

record.status: HOLD: MIT-licensed code and a single best checkpoint in the GitHub repository (licence file in the ProteinTalks subfolder only); training data on Google Drive; Nature article subscription-only.
record.io: Baseline proteomic profile + perturbation descriptor + drug fingerprints/physicochemical features -> predicted proteome at 6/24/48 h and drug efficacy or combination-synergy probability
record.use_cases: Drug efficacy and synergy prediction, drug-combination discovery, resistance-associated protein interpretation, patient/organoid response stratification
record.audit_note: Repository found by code search, not via the paper (Nature full text unreadable); licence only in subfolder; modality for perturbation-proteomics models not yet assigned by curator; released checkpoint is a breast-cancer drug-response model, so scope is borderline.

review.reason: Artifact blocker partly resolved: GitHub code search found the Guo lab (guomics-lab; last author Guo T) repository PTV-1 with a ProteinTalks/ folder holding training/prediction code, an MIT LICENCE.md (copyright 'yonggeli66') and a 10.1 MB best_checkpoint.pth committed 2026-09-04; training data linked on Google Drive. Remaining blockers: (1) the Nature article is still subscription-only and its code-availability statement could not be read, so the paper-to-repository link is unconfirmed (the 2025 bioRxiv preprint text I read cites only db.prottalks.com for data); (2) repo-level licence is undetected by GitHub (licence file sits in the subfolder only); (3) curator modality routing for a bulk perturbation-proteomics neural-ODE model is still open, and scope is borderline: the released checkpoint is the joint proteome-dynamics + drug efficacy/synergy model trained on breast-cancer cell lines. A 2025 bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2025.02.07.637070, v1 2025-02-10, v2 2025-02-12) is the first public version. A third-party 'lattiasg/ProteinTalks' demo repo (created 2026-10-22) was not treated as official.
review.reconsider_when: The Nature code-availability statement (or the repo README) confirms guomics-lab/PTV-1 as the official ProteinTalks release, and the curator assigns a modality and confirms scope for perturbation-proteomics virtual-cell models.

record.name: WILSON
record.description: Mayo Clinic vision-language pathology foundation model built on multi-magnification composite images of slides and cases, trained on about 189,000 slides spanning 42 organs and 829 diagnostic entities with pathology reports as supervision, for patient-level analysis and diagnostic text generation.
record.status: HOLD: No released code or weights; the preprint states the model will be made available for download upon publication, subject to Mayo Clinic Ethics Office clearance.
record.io: H&E whole-slide images rendered as multi-magnification composite images (slide or case level) -> slide/patient embeddings and generated diagnostic text
record.use_cases: Patient-level pathology classification, slide/case retrieval, diagnostic report generation, treatment-response prediction
record.audit_note: Preprint only; no artifact released; release is conditional on publication and ethics clearance; terms unknown (pending patent noted).

review.reason: A v2 was posted 18 Oct 2026; its Code Availability section still promises release only upon publication and subject to Mayo Clinic Ethics Office clearance, and adds a pending US provisional patent. No WILSON model found on Hugging Face. Substantive in-scope slide/case-level pathology model with a stated, checkable release trigger, so it suits the under-review register.
review.reconsider_when: WILSON weights or a documented access route are published with readable licence/access terms.

record.name: Haiku
record.description: Tri-modal contrastive model from the Zhi Huang lab that aligns multiplexed immunofluorescence (CODEX) spatial-proteomics patches, matched H&E histology and clinical-metadata text in one embedding space, trained on 26.7 million mIF patches from 3,218 tissue sections of 1,606 patients across 11 organ types; Haiku(Bi) is a bi-modal H&E-mIF variant without the text encoder.
record.status: HOLD: Code on GitHub with no licence file (all rights reserved by default); weights on Hugging Face behind manual gates with hub licence 'other' and unreadable terms; bundles MUSK, whose own weights are CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0.
record.io: mIF/CODEX patches, H&E patches and clinical-metadata text -> shared tri-modal embeddings; cross-modal retrieval and zero-shot biomarker inference
record.use_cases: Cross-modal retrieval between spatial proteomics, histology and clinical text; survival and clinical prediction; zero-shot biomarker inference from H&E; exploratory counterfactual analysis of tissue niches
record.audit_note: Preprint only; code has no licence; weights manually gated with unreadable terms; noncommercial=true inferred from the bundled MUSK component (CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0), not from Haiku's own terms.

review.reason: Paper blocker resolved: arXiv 2605.00925 (30 Apr 2026; Cui ... Huang Z) is the primary preprint and its Code Availability names github.com/zhihuanglab/Haiku and huggingface.co/zhihuanglab/Haiku (the October lane missed it because the repo citation block is still a placeholder). The bundle ships MUSK, whose hub licence is cc-by-nc-nd-4.0 (manually gated), so non-commercial terms very likely reach at least one component. Haiku_state_dict.pt present in both repos (3.2 GB / 2.8 GB per README).
review.reconsider_when: A licence file is added to the GitHub repository or the Haiku hub card states readable licence/gate terms.

record.name: JEPA-DNA (NV-JEPA-DNA)
record.description: NVIDIA continual-pretraining framework that adds a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture latent-prediction objective (with VICReg-style regularisation) to the native MLM or next-token objective of existing genomic language models. Released checkpoints are JEPA-continued DNABERT-2, HyenaDNA and NTv3-100M backbones trained on OpenGenome2 crops.
record.status: HOLD: Apache-2.0 code; ungated weights under the NVIDIA non-commercial licence (card adds that terms are subject to NVIDIA's internal legal and open-source release review); derivative checkpoints of displayed parents (NTv3, DNABERT-2, HyenaDNA) pending a catalog rule for continual-pretraining derivatives
record.io: DNA sequence (single-nucleotide tokens for the NTv3 variant, up to 8,192 bp) -> token hidden states and mean-pooled sequence embeddings
record.use_cases: Feature extraction and linear probing for genomic classification tasks, zero-shot embedding-based scoring of sequence perturbations, continual-pretraining studies
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06. arXiv v4 (2026-10-15), preprint not peer reviewed. Official repo Apache-2.0; three official checkpoints ungated, NVIDIA non-commercial licence with a pending-release-review clause. Held on scope: derivative checkpoints of displayed parents; decide with DNT and other continual-pretraining derivatives. Community MLX/re-uploads (jbilcke/jepa-dna-mlx, Arsh9210/*) are not official.

review.reason: Substantive and in scope on its own merits: NVIDIA arXiv paper (now v4, 2026-10-15) evaluating 17 genomic tasks; official Apache-2.0 code (GitHub NVIDIA-BioNeMo/JEPA-DNA; the card's NVIDIA-Digital-Bio link redirects there); three official ungated checkpoints (NTv3-100M, DNABERT-2, HyenaDNA backbones) under the NVIDIA non-commercial licence. All three parents are now displayed (bfm-ntv3, bfm-dnabert-2, bfm-hyenadna). The October blocker (no rule on whether continual-pretraining frameworks with derivative checkpoints get their own record) is a maintainer policy decision, still open, so hold on the register rather than accept. Extra terms caveat: the card says the NVIDIA licence applies 'subject to completion of NVIDIA's applicable internal legal and open source release review process'.
review.reconsider_when: Maintainers set a rule for continual-pretraining frameworks whose checkpoints derive from displayed parents (own record versus note on NTv3/DNABERT-2/HyenaDNA); apply it consistently to DNT.

record.name: Vir2vec
record.description: Decoder-only viral genomic language models (17M, 138M and 422M parameters) continually pretrained from Mistral-DNA on 565,747 complete viral genomes across 295 species, used as frozen genome-level embedding extractors. The preprint also introduces the vGUE viral genome-understanding benchmark and a codon-level SHAP attribution method.
record.status: HOLD: weights tagged MIT on Hugging Face but behind a manual gate (files on request with institutional e-mail, intended use and IRB protocol number); training-code repository has no licence; parent Mistral-DNA is itself on hold
record.io: Complete viral genome sequence -> 4,096-dimensional genome-level embeddings
record.use_cases: Viral taxonomy and genus-level discrimination, variant subtyping, host-tropism prediction from frozen embeddings, zero-shot generalisation to unseen viral families, viral surveillance pipelines
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06. Preprint v4, not peer reviewed. Weights manually gated with an IRB-number request; MIT tag on the card, but gate conditions add access requirements; files not inspected beyond the API listing. GitHub code has no licence (all rights reserved by default). Derivative of held Mistral-DNA; noncommercial=false reflects the MIT tag only and is not proof of permissive access.

review.reason: Substantive in-scope viral gLM family (17M/138M/422M; preprint v4 2026-09-24 with the vGUE benchmark and frozen-embedding evaluation across 7 tasks). Of the three October blockers, one is now partly resolved: the gate conditions are readable on the card (share HF info; files on request with institutional e-mail, intended-use description and IRB protocol number). Still open: the GitHub training-code repo has no licence (license null, unchanged since 2026-09-22), and the parent Mistral-DNA remains on hold (bfm-mistral-dna). Card tags MIT for weights. Hold on the register with multiple specific blockers.
review.reconsider_when: The GitHub repository carries a licence, the gate is lifted or reduced to standard terms, and the Mistral-DNA parent hold (bfm-mistral-dna) is resolved.

record.name: PhaGen
record.description: Hierarchical masked-diffusion model for bacteriophage DNA (152,421,601 parameters; three stages of dimension 512/256/196 over a 131,072-token canvas) that generates DNA on a masked canvas rather than left to right, so the same weights yield unconditional sequence generation, 964-dimensional sequence representations and masked conditional scores. Trained on 98,665 phage genomes (about 4.8 Gb) from MGV, GPD and NCBI.
record.status: HOLD: Open weights + custom model code on Hugging Face, ungated, Apache-2.0 declared in the card and a full LICENSE file; adapted files also carry upstream MIT (MEGABYTE) and Apache-2.0 (Open-dLLM) terms per NOTICE.md; no paper, no training corpus release, no API
record.io: Phage DNA sequence as single-nucleotide tokens (9-token vocabulary, canvas up to 131,072 tokens) -> masked-token logits, 964-dimensional sequence embeddings and diffusion-sampled DNA contigs
record.use_cases: Unconditional phage genome generation, frozen sequence representations for downstream probes, masked conditional scoring of phage DNA
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06. No paper or preprint exists for this model as far as could be checked: the card and NOTICE.md refer to 'the paper' and to a 'frozen paper artifact' without a citation, and arXiv (all:PhaGen) and Europe PMC (masked diffusion AND phage, including SRC:PPR) returned nothing. The repository examined in October (Tim419/PhaGen) now returns 401; the model now sits at YusenWithR/PhaGen, created 2026-10-15, and identity rests on matching card content (same 152,421,601 parameters, same stage/canvas table, same NOTICE structure), not on a stated author list. Licence and corpus blockers from October are resolved: Apache-2.0 card field plus full LICENSE, upstream MEGABYTE/Open-dLLM/VeOmni provenance documented, corpus stated. NOTICE.md adds that the Apache-2.0 grant makes no claim over the training datasets, which keep their own terms, and describes the weights as 'released for research use'; that phrase sits beside an unqualified Apache-2.0 grant and was not treated as a non-commercial restriction. Weights were not downloaded or run; benchmark claims are not independently checkable without a paper.

review.reason: Two of the three October blockers are resolved, on a different hub repository. The October repository Tim419/PhaGen now returns HTTP 401 for both the web page and the API; a repository YusenWithR/PhaGen (created 2026-10-15, last modified 2026-10-18) carries the same model (identical 152,421,601 parameter count and the same architecture table as the October excerpt), now with cardData license apache-2.0, a full Apache-2.0 LICENSE file, a NOTICE.md that resolves the upstream MEGABYTE (MIT) and Open-dLLM (Apache-2.0) provenance left open in October, a stated training corpus (98,665 phage genomes, 4,800,631,119 bases from MGV, GPD and NCBI), and an ungated model.safetensors. The remaining blocker is the paper: the card repeatedly refers to 'the paper' and NOTICE.md calls the weights 'the frozen paper artifact', but nothing cites or links one. An arXiv API full-text query for PhaGen returned zero hits, as did Europe PMC queries for PhaGen and for masked-diffusion phage preprints (SRC:PPR). Secondary caveat: the account change between the October and current repositories is unexplained, so authorship rests on card content matching, not on a stated author list; the card names no authors beyond 'The PhaGen authors'. In scope as a dna model (unconditional generation, sequence representations via model.embed, masked conditional scoring) and substantive, so it belongs on the register rather than staying a bare lead.
review.reconsider_when: A paper or preprint for PhaGen is published and cited from the hub card (or the authors are otherwise named), so model identity and the 'frozen paper artifact' claim can be tied to a primary source.

record.name: scKITE
record.description: Single-cell transcriptomic Transformer encoder trained in two stages: masked encoder pretraining, then multi-task training that adds cell-annotation and gene-regulatory (regulon) supervision through lightweight auxiliary decoders over a joint gene/text vocabulary. Released as one Stage 2 checkpoint from the 50% geosketch pretraining run.
record.status: HOLD: MIT code on GitHub; one ungated Stage 2 checkpoint (best.pt, 2.36 GB, SHA-256 published in the README) and benchmark/pretraining datasets on Hugging Face, but the hub repository carries no model card or licence and the README states the MIT grant does not cover weights, datasets or tokenizers; Stage 1 checkpoint not released
record.io: Single-cell RNA-seq expression over the bundled joint gene/text vocabulary -> cell and gene-token representations; with the released heads, batch-integration embeddings, cell-type annotations and GEARS-based perturbation predictions
record.use_cases: Zero-shot batch integration, cell-type annotation, gene-perturbation prediction with GEARS-based adapters, attention-based interpretation of regulatory structure
record.audit_note: Re-reviewed 2026-11-06 against the arXiv v1 record, the GitHub README (commit 'Document released checkpoint and datasets', 2026-10-16) and the Hugging Face API. The Stage 2 checkpoint is now public and ungated, and its size and SHA-256 are published in the README, but the hub repository has no card (raw README.md 404, cardData null), so the weights carry no declared licence; the README's own License section excludes weights, datasets and tokenizers from the MIT code grant. Maturity limits stated by the authors: repository 'under active release preparation', dependency manifests preliminary, Stage 1 checkpoint and the vocabulary revision matching the released checkpoint unpublished, dataset provenance/licences/checksums still being compiled, end-to-end reproducibility tests pending, and a request not to redistribute the bundled resources. Benchmarks are author-reported; no weights were downloaded or run. noncommercial set false because no non-commercial term was seen, not because a permissive licence covers the weights. Attribution rests on the arXiv author list (Jie Bao) matching the BaoJiee GitHub and Baojiecau hub handles; the hub repository does not cite the paper.

review.reason: The October artifact blocker is resolved, and a terms blocker replaces it. A commit on 2026-10-16 ('Document released checkpoint and datasets') added a Model checkpoints section naming a released Stage 2 checkpoint with an exact size (2,355,226,205 bytes) and SHA-256, and the hub repository Baojiecau/scKITE (created 2026-10-16) lists stage2_geosketch_50_20260814_085748/best.pt, ungated and not private. The blocker is now the weight terms: the hub repository has no card at all (raw README.md returns 404) and its cardData is null, so no licence is declared for the weights, and the GitHub README states explicitly that the MIT source-code licence does not extend to model weights, datasets or tokenizers. Maturity caveats also persist in the same README: the repository is 'under active release preparation', the Stage 1 checkpoint and the exact vocabulary revision tied to the released checkpoint are not published, and dataset provenance, licences and checksums are still being compiled. Substantive and in scope (single-cell transcriptomic encoder used for batch integration, annotation, perturbation prediction and interpretation), so it belongs on the register with a checkable terms blocker. This mirrors the OmniTCR treatment in the same batch: public ungated weights with no stated weight licence are held, not accepted.
review.reconsider_when: The Hugging Face repository publishes a model card stating licence terms for the Stage 2 weights (or the GitHub README states weight terms explicitly), ideally alongside the Stage 1 checkpoint and the matching vocabulary revision.

review.reason: The terms blocker is unchanged. record.name: MitoSpace (MitoSpace4D)
